web.description:
# Add These Beautiful Beaches in Japan to Your Itinerary
### SHARE
##### Share
###### SHARE
- [Kuroshima Venus Road (黒島ヴィーナスロード) — one of the most romantic Japanese beaches](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches.html#sec06_02)

- [Chichibugahama Beach (父母ヶ浜) — stunning beach renowned for its unique sandbar and picturesque scenery](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches.html#sec07_02)

- [Miyako Island (宮古島) — home to several breathtaking beaches, including Yoshino, Sunayama, Maehama](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches.html#sec08_03)
- [Ishigaki Island (石垣島) — home to picturesque beaches like Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches.html#sec08_04)

## The best beaches in the Kyushu region
Okinawa also has some of the most beautiful beaches in the world.

### Ishigaki Island (石垣島) — home to picturesque beaches like Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach
![Ishigaki Island (石垣島) — home to picturesque beaches like Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_319632984.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717870.jpeg)

It also has several beautiful sandy and rocky beaches, snorkeling areas, and diving spots.

With emerald blue waters, Kabira Bay is known as Ishigaki’s most scenic view. Yonehara Beach is covered with white corals, and its reef is a beautiful place to go snorkeling and diving.

## The best beaches in the Hokkaido region

As the northernmost region in Japan, Hokkaido is famous for its rugged outdoors, fine powdery snow, and delicious food. For travelers asking, “Are there beaches in Japan’s northern regions?” the answer is yes. Hokkaido has beautiful beaches that are unique from other beaches in Japan.

### Shimamui Beach (島武意海岸) — boasting of rugged cliffs and a rocky coastline

![Shimamui Beach (島武意海岸) — boasting of rugged cliffs and a rocky coastline](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_2085435189_cop_1574372118.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717505.jpeg)

Shimamui Beach, located in Bikuni, is a must-visit when in Hokkaido. Rugged cliffs and rocky coastlines are the main attraction, allowing visitors a glimpse of Japan’s stunning beauty — and beyond it, the Sea of Japan. The water comes in various shades of blue, inviting tourists to explore its depths by swimming, snorkeling, and even scuba diving.

**How to get to Shimamui Beach:** Fly to New Chitose Airport. Take a Rapid Airport transfer to Otaru Station. Walk to the Otaru Eki Mae bus station and ride the 21 Shakotan Sen bus line to Shimamui Kaigan Iriguchi. Walk for 10–15 minutes to reach the beach.

### Tokoro Jonan Beach (常南ビーチ海水浴場) — snow-covered winter spectacle

![Tokoro Jonan Beach (常南ビーチ海水浴場) — snow-covered winter spectacle](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_2047275859_cop_1068018227.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717521.jpeg)

During the summer, Tokoro Beach is a popular destination for swimming and sunbathing. What makes it different from other beaches, however, is how snow covers the beach during the colder months. Visitors can stroll along the snow-draped shoreline and experience winter activities like skiing and snowboarding.

**How to get to Tokoro Jonan Beach:** Fly to Memanbetsu Airport. Take the Memanbetsu Airport Line to Harowaku-mae. Switch to the Tokoro Line and get off at Tokoro Shokohkaikan. Walk to the beach.

## The best beaches in the Tohoku region

Majestic ocean views, serene lakes, and roaring waterfalls are among the top attractions in Tohoku. While the area is particularly stunning in the spring and fall, Tohoku has several beaches you mustn't miss during the summer.

### Jodogahama Beach (浄土ヶ浜) — a little paradise outside the city center

![Jodogahama Beach (浄土ヶ浜) — a little paradise outside the city center](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_2047275859_cop_181622884.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717548.jpeg)

Also called "Pure Land Beach," Jodogahama is one of the most famous places for beautiful scenic spots because of its clear, calm waters in contrast with its white, pebbled shoreline. Lying outside central Miyako City, this popular tourist spot is a part of the Sanriku Recovery National Park along the Sanriku Coast.

**How to get to Jodogahama Beach:** Fly to Iwate Hanamaki Airport. Take the Hanamaki-Airport Limousine Bus to Morioka Station. Get on the 106 Tokkyu Bus to Jodogahama Park Hotel Mae station. Walk for about 10 minutes to get to the beach.

### Tanesashi Coast (種差海岸) — natural grass on the water’s edge

![Tanesashi Coast (種差海岸) — natural grass on the water’s edge](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_2047275859_cop.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717564.jpeg)

Tanesashi Coast is part of the Sanriku Fukko National Park. Its proximity to the city center makes it accessible to visitors who want to surf, swim, or walk along the coast of Japan. Along the coastline, you may find some parts where natural grass grows along the water’s edge. In other parts, you can walk on the nakisuna (singing sand), which makes a sound when stepped on. Nearby, you’ll find a vast plain where you can see various flora and fauna.

**How to get to Tanesashi Coast:** Fly to Misawa Airport. Take the Misawa-Airport Limousine Bus and get off at Hon-Hachinohe Station. Ride the Hachinohe Line to Okuki Station. The beach is a 6-minute walk from the station.

## The best beaches in the Kanto region

The Kanto region is home to big cities like Tokyo and Yokohama. Also, Hakone is a popular weekend destination famous for its onsen (hot springs) and ryokan (traditional inns). You’ll also find several sandy beaches that are the go-to destination for those who want a quick getaway.

### Yuigahama Beach (由比ヶ浜海岸) — surfing beach with calm waves

![Yuigahama Beach (由比ヶ浜海岸) — surfing beach with calm waves](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_279376162.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717591.jpeg)

Yuigahama Beach has always seen large crowds during the swimming season, even during the Meiji period. It is a famous beach where the children can swim safely, as the water is shallow and the waves are relatively calm. Recently, it has become a popular destination for surfers.

**How to get to Yuigahama Beach:** Take the Skyliner to Keisei Ueno Station from Narita International Airport. Walk to Ueno Station and ride the Ueno-Tokyo Line until Totsuka Station. Transfer to the Yokosuka Line and get off at Kamakura Station. Ride the Enoden Line until the Wadazuka Station. Walk about four minutes to get to Yuigahama Beach.

### Zaimokuza Beach (材木座海水浴場) — a favorite spot near Tokyo for locals and visitors

![Zaimokuza Beach (材木座海水浴場) — a favorite spot near Tokyo for locals and visitors](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_279376162_copy.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717607.jpeg)

With its long, shallow shore and gentle waves, Zaimokuza is a favorite beach spot among locals and tourists. Its proximity to Tokyo makes it easy to visit, and it has the longest shoreline among the three swimming beaches in Kamakura City. Rent a beach house and life vests, and spend an entire day swimming and relaxing to your heart's content.

**How to get to Zaimokuza Beach:** Take the Skyliner to Keisei Ueno Station from Narita International Airport. Walk to Ueno Station and ride the Ueno-Tokyo Line until Totsuka Station. Transfer to the Yokosuka Line and get off at Kamakura Station. Walk to the Kamakura Eki bus stop and ride until Zaimokuza. The beach is a four-minute walk from the bus station.

### Oarai Sun Beach (大洗サンビーチ海水浴場) — the family-friendly beach of Ibaraki Prefecture

![Oarai Sun Beach (大洗サンビーチ海水浴場) — the family-friendly beach of Ibaraki Prefecture](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717624.jpeg)

Oarai Sun Beach is one of Ibaraki’s most famous destinations, especially during the summer when it attracts thousands of visitors daily. Popular because of its clear, sparkling sands and shallow waters, it is the perfect getaway for families. Surfers and swimmers test the gentle waves every summer. Other attractions include beach volleyball, surfing contests, and other fun-filled marine activities.

**How to get to Oarai Sun Beach:** Take the Skyliner to Nippori Station from Narita International Airport. Hop on the Yamanote Line until Ueno Station. Ride the JR Hitachi and Tokiwa Express until Mito Station. Switch to the Kashimarinkai Tetsudo Oara-Kashima Line and get off at Oarai Station. Walk for about 20 minutes to get to the beach.

## The best beaches in the Chubu region

When you visit the Chubu region, you’ll find many mountainous areas. It is the home of Mt. Fuji, Japan’s tallest mountain, and Hida and Kisa, other high mountain ranches. Chubu also has some of the best beaches.

### Shirahama Beach (白浜) — a popular beach in summer

![Shirahama Beach (白浜) — a popular beach in summer](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717650.jpeg)

Known for good surfing conditions and peaceful waters, Shirahama Beach is one of the most popular attractions in the area. People come to sunbathe, surf, and swim, making it one of the most crowded beaches, especially during the swimming season. It is also famous for spectacular sunsets, sparkling turquoise waters, and white sands.

**How to get to Shirahama Beach:** Take the Narita Express to Shinagawa Station from Narita International Airport. Ride the Tokaido-Sanyo bullet train to Atami Station and switch to JJR Odoriko limited express train. Get off at Izukyu Shimoda and ride the Itado Isshiki Bus until the Shirahama Beach bus stop.

### Sotoura Beach (外浦ビーチ) — a quiet, less crowded beach

![Sotoura Beach (外浦ビーチ) — a quiet, less crowded beach](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717666.jpeg)

Clear waters and a bright sun await your adventure in Sotoura Beach, a quiet beach spot in the Shizuoka Prefecture. Its closeness to Tokyo makes it a popular weekend getaway for people looking to spend a few days basking in the sun and sand. While it is the perfect spot for swimming, snorkeling, kayaking, and sunbathing, Sotoura Beach is less populated, unlike neighboring beaches, Shirahama and Shirahama Ohama.

**How to get to Sotoura Beach:** Take the Narita Express to Shinagawa Station from Narita International Airport. Ride the Tokaido-Sanyo bullet train to Atami Station and switch to JJR Odoriko limited express train. Get off at Izukyu Shimoda and ride the Itado Isshiki Bus until Waipoku. Walk to the beach.

## The best beaches in the Kansai region

Kansai, Japan’s cultural and religious capital, is filled with zen gardens, ancient castles, and other historical sites. It is also home to several beaches with stunning views.

### Shirarahama Beach (白良浜) — popular for soft, white sand and clear blue waters

![Shirarahama Beach (白良浜) — popular for soft, white sand and clear blue waters](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717692.jpeg)

Shirarahama Beach (not to be confused with Shirahama Beach in Shizuoka Prefecture) is a white sand resort dubbed the “sister beach” of Waikiki Beach in Hawaii. Known as one of the top beach resort areas in the Kansai region, Shirarahama has a long stretch of white sandy shores and beautiful blue waves. Nearby are other attractions, such as Senjojiki, a tiered rock formation, a leisure park, and several hot springs resorts.

**How to get to Shirarahama Beach:** Take the Kansaikuko Line to Shirahama Station from Kansai International Airport. Switch to the 12 Shirahama Tanabe Line and get off at Shirarahama Beach.

### Keino Matsubara Beach (慶野松原) — see beautiful sunsets from a pine forest

![Keino Matsubara Beach (慶野松原) — see beautiful sunsets from a pine forest](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_674803608.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717708.jpeg)

Located in Minamiawaji City, Keino Matsubara has a quiet scenic charm that attracts visitors from different places. Spread out in front of the beach are thousands of black pines. You can come for a swim during the day, but be sure to stay until evening as the sunset across the Harima Sea is truly spectacular and one of the best sunsets in Japan.

**How to get to Keino Matsubara Beach:** Take the Haruka Express to Osaka Station from Kansai International Airport. Hop on the Tokaido-Sanyo Line to Sannomiya Station. Make your way to the bus terminal and get on the Kobe - Minamiawaji bus to Riku no Minato Seidan. Switch to the Torikai bus and ride until Keino Matsubara.

## The best beaches in the Chugoku region

While famous for its history and floating shrine, Chugoku has plenty to see and do. You can visit idyllic seaside towns and go island-hopping on the Seto Inland Sea. Some of its beaches are particularly stunning and a must-visit when you’re in the region.

### Kikugahama Beach (菊ケ浜海水浴場)— spectacular sunset views

![Kikugahama Beach (菊ケ浜海水浴場)— spectacular sunset views](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_1135533460.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717736.jpeg)

Kikugahama Beach, located in the Kita-Nagato Kaigan Quasi-National Park, has peaceful views of the Sizuki mountains and other islands that dot the ocean. Chosen as one of the best swimming beaches, it is a popular summer destination for those who want to swim or watch the sunset.

**How to get to Kikugahama Beach:** Fly to Hiroshima Airport. From there, take the Hiroshima Airport Limousine Bus to Hiroshima Station. Hop on the Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen and ride to Shin-Yamaguchi Station. Get on the Higashihagi bus until Hagi Meirin Center. Walk for about 20 minutes to get to the beach.

### Kuroshima Venus Road (黒島ヴィーナスロード) — one of the most romantic Japanese beaches

![Kuroshima Venus Road (黒島ヴィーナスロード) — one of the most romantic Japanese beaches](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_1497730936.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717752.jpeg)

Kuroshima Venus Road is more of a sandbar than a beach. During the low tide, it connects Kuroshima Island, Nakanoko Island, and Hashinokojima Island on the Seto Inland Sea. When the water goes down, you can trek from one island to another. Keep a lookout for heart-shaped stones as you stroll along the sandy path.

**How to get to Kuroshima Venus Road:** From Okayama Momotaro Airport, take the Okayama Airport Limousine Bus to Okayama Station. Ride the Ako Line and get off at Saidaiji Station. Get on the Ushimado Bus until Olive-en Iriguchi. Walk to Hotel Limani, where you can get on a boat or sightseeing ship to Kuroshima Venus Road and its three islands.

## The best beaches in the Shikoku region

While Shikoku is most famous for the 88 Temple Pilgrimage, you will also find many beautiful nature spots around the area, including valleys, streams, and beaches.

### Katsurahama Beach (桂浜) — known for its scenic beauty and cultural significance

![Katsurahama Beach (桂浜) — known for its scenic beauty and cultural significance](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_288015533.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717778.jpeg)

Just 30 minutes south of central Kochi is Katsurahama lies a beach with beautiful scenic views. Because of the strong currents, swimming isn’t allowed, but there are many things to do. Nearby is a statue of Sakamoto Ryoma, one of the architects of modern Japan who helped end Japan’s feudal age in 1868. Also near the beach is the Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum and other pleasant walking paths, tourist spots, and local restaurants that serve delicious food.

**How to get to Katsurahama Beach:** From Matsuyama Airport, ride the Matsuyama Airport Line to Kochi Eki Bus Terminal. Switch to the Katsurahama Line and get off at Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum. Walk for about five minutes to get to the beach.

### Chichibugahama Beach (父母ヶ浜) — stunning beach renowned for its unique sandbar and picturesque scenery

![Chichibugahama Beach (父母ヶ浜) — stunning beach renowned for its unique sandbar and picturesque scenery](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_1848726462.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717795.jpeg)

Stretching over one kilometer long, Chichibugahama Beach recently became famous for having a sandbar where tourists can take mirror photos. Many visitors come to catch the sunset reflecting on the low-tide pools that form in the sand where no wind disturbs the water's surface.

**How to get to Chichibugahama Beach:** From Matsuyama Airport, ride the Matsuyama Airport Line to Matsuyama Station. Switch to the Yosan Line-Limited Express and ride until Kan-Onji Station. Transfer to the Yosan Line until Takuma Station. Walk to the Takuma Eki Bus stop and ride 11. Nio Line until Tenno. Walk for about three minutes to Chichibugahama Beach.

## The best beaches in the Kyushu region

Famous for pristine beaches, diving spots, and beautiful nature scenes, Okinawa has been dubbed the “Hawaii of Japan.” It comprises over 160 islands, some covered with thick trees, flowing rivers, and majestic waterfalls. Okinawa also has some of the most beautiful beaches in the world.

### Yurigahama Beach (百合ヶ浜) — featuring a stunning sandbar that appears and disappears with the tide

![Yurigahama Beach (百合ヶ浜) — featuring a stunning sandbar that appears and disappears with the tide](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_1937818882.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717821.jpeg)

Yurigahama Beach, situated off the coast of Yoron Island, has a unique phenomenon known as the mysterious yet magical “beach within a beach.” When the tide is low, a large, sandy oasis appears where visitors can swim and snorkel. Made of tiny corals and surrounded by clear waters, it has earned its nickname, “Phantasmal Beach.”

**How to get to Yurigahama Beach:** Fly to Yoron Island. You can take a taxi to the beach or drive a rented car from the airport.

### Nishihama Beach (ニシ浜ビーチ) — pristine white sand and turquoise waters

![Nishihama Beach (ニシ浜ビーチ) — pristine white sand and turquoise waters](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_708786202.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717837.jpeg)

Located in the northwest part of Hateruma Island, the southernmost inhabited island in the Okinawa chain, Nishihama’s blue waters have earned themselves the name “Hateruma Blue.” Close to the white, sandy shore, the waves are a beautiful turquoise shade but gradually get darker as they extend toward the ocean. Said to be the most beautiful beach in Okinawa, it has a white sandy shore that stretches endlessly, and its waters are the perfect place to swim, snorkel in, or gather seashells.

**How to get to Nishihama Beach:** Fly to Ishigaki Airport on Ishigaki Island. Take the Ishigaki Airport Limousine Bus to Ishigaki Port. From there, you can get a high-speed ferry to Hateruma Island. The beach is a few minutes walk away from the port.

### Miyako Island (宮古島) — home to several breathtaking beaches, including Yoshino, Sunayama, Maehama

![Miyako Island (宮古島) — home to several breathtaking beaches, including Yoshino, Sunayama, Maehama](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_467825802.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717854.jpeg)

If you travel some 300 kilometers south of Okinawa Main Island, you may find yourself on Miyako Island, the fourth largest island of Okinawa Prefecture. Miyako’s most famous attraction is its picturesque beaches which provide a fascinating destination for relaxing, swimming, and snorkeling.

Maehama, one of its beaches, is famous for its beautiful sunsets and water sports activities. Yoshino Beach is known for swarms of colorful fish when you go swimming. Sunayama Beach has clear white sand and fascinating rock formations.

**How to get to Miyako Island:** Fly from Tokyo to Miyako Airport. From there, you’ll be able to find buses that take you to the different beaches.

### Ishigaki Island (石垣島) — home to picturesque beaches like Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach

![Ishigaki Island (石垣島) — home to picturesque beaches like Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach](https://www.jal.co.jp/ar/en/guide-to-japan/destinations/articles/multi/japans-best-beaches/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/sectioncontainer_cop/image_copy_copy_copy_319632984.coreimg.jpeg/1776760717870.jpeg)

Home to Okinawa Prefecture’s highest mountain, Ishigaki Island is a scenic island filled with jungle-like scenery and hiking trails. It also has several beautiful sandy and rocky beaches, snorkeling areas, and diving spots.

With emerald blue waters, Kabira Bay is known as Ishigaki’s most scenic view. While you can't swim, snorkel or dive, you can ride on a glass-bottom boat to catch a glimpse of the underwater world. Yonehara Beach is covered with white corals, and its reef is a beautiful place to go snorkeling and diving.

**How to get to Ishigaki Island:** Fly to Ishigaki Airport. From there, you’ll be able to find bus transfers to Kabira Bay and Yonehara Beach. They are a few minutes walk from each other.

## Transcript

You might think that Tokyo doesn't have any decent beaches, and that's because you're thinking
of Tokyo like this. What most people don't know is that the prefecture of Tokyo actually extends all
the way out to include a bunch of islands south of the mainland. Some of these islands are home to
wild, untamed nature, and some of them, like Niijima, have the clearest water and best beaches I've
ever seen in my nine years living in Japan. This tiny island actually blew me away. And the best
part is that it's only three hours away from Tokyo by boat. It's actually really cool because
it's a jet foil boat, so we're going really, really fast, but it's really smooth.
We just picked up the rental car, actually, the owner of the hostel/hotel that we're staying
at tonight. They just came and, like, picked us up from the terminal just because they're kind, which
is really nice. It's way hotter here than Tokyo. It feels like, I don't know, like the sun is stronger
for sure, which is perfect for the beach. it's a beautiful day. So excited.
Chris and I both hiked Fuji yesterday. Mistakes were made. Oh boy.
Oh, look at that. Look at that line. Maybe it's better in the shade? I don't know. Oh, ouch. The shame I
feel as an Australian to get a sunburn. It's crazy. I feel so guilty. What's wrong with me? It's
supposed to be a really nice, like, observatory over here. It's about 40 minutes walk away. You can
drive there, but I've heard it's like a nice hike, so let's see.
Whoa!
Whoa! Hot damn. That's beautiful. Oh, my gosh, look at that water.
Why are you standing like that?
This car is way too small for this. It really looks like we're not supposed to be down this street. But this is

## Explore Beaches in Okinawa, Tokyo, Izu & More

# Best Beaches in Japan

The best beaches in Japan include Emerald Beach in Okinawa, Shirahama Beach in Wakayama, Ohama Beach in Amami Oshima and Zushi Beach near Tokyo, offering white sand, coral reefs, calm swimming and surf spots across some of Asia’s most underrated coastlines.


* * *

Updated: July 23, 2026

Japan may be famous for temples, sushi and cherry blossoms—but its beaches are some of the most underrated coastal escapes in Asia. With crystal-clear waters, coral reefs, white sand and lush island backdrops, the best beaches in Japan rival tropical destinations across the Pacific. Whether you’re looking for snorkeling spots, tranquil swimming coves or a scenic beach near a major city, Japan has something for every traveler.

Some of the best beaches in Japan include Emerald Beach in Okinawa, Shirahama Beach in Wakayama, Amami Oshima’s Ohama Beach and Zushi Beach near Tokyo. From the tropical shores of the Ryukyu Islands to the rugged coastlines of the Izu Peninsula, here’s where to find the top beaches in Japan by region and traveler type.

## Best Beaches in Okinawa

### 1\. Emerald Beach: Best For Families and Calm Swimming

Located in Okinawa’s Ocean Expo Park, Emerald Beach is one of the best family-friendly beaches in Japan. Divided into three sections—“playground,” “rest,” and “view”—this curved shoreline offers lifeguards, calm swimming areas and incredible views of emerald-colored water. It’s clean, safe and easy to access, making it a favorite for those traveling with kids.

### 2\. Yurigahama Beach: Best For Scenic Sandbars and Shallow Wading

Accessible only at low tide, Yurigahama is a floating sandbar off Yoron Island that appears like magic in the middle of the ocean. With water so clear it looks like glass and soft white sand beneath your feet, this is one of Japan’s most unique and photogenic beaches. It’s especially popular for wading, drone photography and scenic boat rides.

### 3\. Kondoi Beach: Best For Peaceful Swimming and Island Views

On the small, traditional island of Taketomi, Kondoi Beach offers calm, shallow water perfect for floating or strolling along the sandbar. It’s one of the quietest beaches in the Okinawa chain and ideal for travelers looking to unwind. Bring a picnic and enjoy the postcard-worthy view of neighboring islands in the distance.

### 4\. Yonaha Maehama Beach: Best For Romantic Sunsets and Powder-Soft Sand

Located on Miyako Island, Yonaha Maehama stretches for over four miles and is often ranked among Japan’s most beautiful beaches. Its soft, flour-like sand and calm waters make it great for swimming and the sunsets here are spectacular. It's a popular beach for honeymooners and photographers.

## Best Beaches in Mainland Japan

### 1\. Shirahama Beach (Wakayama): Best For White Sand and Hot Springs

Shirahama Beach in Wakayama Prefecture is one of the best beaches near Osaka and Kyoto, featuring imported white sand from Australia. It offers clear water, beachfront hot spring resorts and family-friendly vibes. After a swim, you can soak in ocean-view onsens or stroll the beachside promenade.

### 2\. Zushi Beach (Kanagawa): Best For Tokyo Travelers and Local Flavor

Just over an hour from central Tokyo, Zushi Beach is a favorite weekend getaway for city dwellers. While not tropical, it offers clean sand, shallow water and views of Mount Fuji on a clear day. It’s a popular spot for paddleboarding and barbecues, with local restaurants lining the beachfront.

### 3\. Tatadohama Beach (Izu Peninsula): Best For Surfing and Beach Breaks

Tatadohama Beach is one of Japan’s top surf spots, located on the southern coast of the Izu Peninsula. It’s known for consistent waves, dramatic coastline and a laid-back surf town vibe. Whether you’re catching waves or just relaxing on the sand, this beach combines adventure with coastal charm.

## Best Beaches in the Amami Islands

### 1\. Ohama Beach (Amami Oshima): Best For Snorkeling and Coral Reefs

Ohama Beach on Amami Oshima is part of a protected nature zone and offers excellent snorkeling right from shore. Coral reefs, tropical fish and sea turtles are just offshore and the surrounding forest adds a lush, wild feel. It’s one of the best beaches in Japan for underwater adventure without the crowds.

## Shore Excursions to Japan’s Beaches

Shore excursions in Japan often include visits to beaches near cultural landmarks or island escapes. Depending on your port, options may include:

- **Okinawa Beach Day**: Relax at Emerald Beach or explore nearby coral coves
- **Izu Peninsula Coastal Tour**: Visit Tatadohama and other beach towns from Shimizu or Yokohama
- **Amami Island Adventure**: Snorkel at Ohama Beach and explore the island’s nature preserves
- **Shirahama Beach & Hot Springs**: Combine a swim with a relaxing soak in a seaside onsen

## Quick List of Top Beaches by Traveler Type

Emerald Beach (Okinawa Main Island) – Best for family-friendly beach days

- **Yurigahama Beach (Yoron Island) –** Best for scenic beauty and sandbar views
- **Shirahama Beach (Wakayama) –** Best for hot springs and white sand
- **Ohama Beach (Amami Oshima) –** Best for snorkeling and coral reef access
- **Zushi Beach (Kanagawa) –** Best for Tokyo day-trippers
- **Tatadohama Beach (Izu Peninsula) –** Best for surfing in Japan
- **Kondoi Beach (Taketomi Island) –** Best for calm swimming and peaceful walks
- **Yonaha Maehama Beach (Miyako Island) –** Best for romantic sunsets and soft sand

## FAQs About Japan’s Beaches:

## 1\. What is the best beach in Japan for families?

The best family-friendly beach in Japan is Emerald Beach in Okinawa. It has calm, shallow water, lifeguards and amenities perfect for visiting with kids.

## 2\. Which beach in Japan is best for couples or honeymoons?

Yonaha Maehama Beach is best for couples and honeymoons. Its soft sand and incredible sunsets make it one of the most romantic beaches in Japan.

## 3\. Where can you go snorkeling in Japan?

One of the best snorkeling beaches in Japan is Ohama Beach on Amami Oshima. Reefs and tropical fish are just offshore, with calm waters ideal for swimming.

## 4\. What is the closest beach to Tokyo?

Zushi Beach in Kanagawa is the closest beach to Tokyo. It’s just over an hour away and offers a relaxed setting with shallow water and mountain views.

## 5\. Are there quiet beaches in Japan that aren’t crowded?

Yes, Kondoi Beach on Taketomi and Tatadohama Beach in Izu are quiet beaches in Japan. Both are scenic, peaceful and less crowded than popular resort areas.

## 6\. What is the most beautiful beach in Japan?

Yurigahama is often called the most beautiful beach in Japan. This seasonal sandbar off Yoron Island appears at low tide and is surrounded by crystal-clear water.

### [And it was more amazing than I could have imagined.](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g1022438-d1161271-r1071429612-Miyajima-Hatsukaichi_Hiroshima_Prefecture_Chugoku.html)









We used to talk about Miyajima, I think we'd like to go there someday, but we didn't get the chance. This is the word of mouth when I visited here last September.

When we started planning, we were a little confused about choosing a hotel because the island where Itsukushima Shrine is located was called "Miyajima" and the opposite shore was called "Miyajima".

To summarize,

● Itsukushima: a remote island under the official name of the island

Miyajima: Another name for Itsukushima. Widely used as a tourist destination name

● Itsukushima Shrine: A World Heritage Site in Itsukushima (= Miyajima)

● Opposite shore (Miyajimaguchi): Around the ferry dock. This place is also sometimes called "Miyajima"



On the way, we took a ferry from Miyajimaguchi to Miyajima (Itsukushima) and on the way back we took another ferry route and stayed at Hiroshima Grand Prince Hotel, which is directly connected to the pier. However, the number of trains was small, and we decided to schedule it according to the ship's time.

There are quite a few trains bound for Miyajimaguchi.



It is a walking distance from the pier to Itsukushima Shrine, while watching the shops lining the approach, but at this time it was difficult to walk because of my elderly mother, and although I had originally heard that there were only a few taxis on the island, when I got to the pier it started to rain heavily.

Under normal circumstances, if a taxi was waiting at the pier, no taxi could come, and when I contacted the taxi company, they said, 'Ask a shared taxi,' but they refused, and I called the taxi company again and again, and managed to get on. You need to be careful when you go with the elderly.

The weather cleared up in about an hour, and a taxi arrived on the way home, which was very helpful.



Itsukushima Shrine has completely different scenery depending on the high tide and low tide.

This time it was low tide, so you can only walk to the Great Torii at low tide.

We didn't go to the torii, but the contrast with people is overwhelming.

A resident who boarded the ferry bound for

He told me that Itsukushima at night was so beautiful that I should come back, and when I actually visited the site, I thought that I would like to stay at a hotel on the side of Itsukushima Shrine and spend some time on the island.

If you stay on the island, you will be able to enjoy the tranquility of the morning and evening and the ebb and flow of the tides, and there seemed to be a lot to see as well as Itsukushima Shrine.

(I was going to ride the ropeway.

Due to heavy rain and lightning, service was suspended.)

Visiting Hashima Island took a bit of effort to plan, so if it's something you're planning on seeing, I would recommend booking early. We tried booking our trip the week of Christmas week about 2 weeks in advance, and found only a few spots left on Klook. We had to move around our itinerary a bit around the available slots. About 2 days after we booked and paid, we were notified that our tour was cancelled. So we scrambled to find another operator, Gunkanjima Cruise Co, (you have to book through one of the few companies that do the boat tours there). The site is a bit outdated, so we werent sure if the booking went through, especially since payment is cash only on-site.



After we booked, we werent even sure if the trip was going to happen. The tours are weather dependent, as the seas around Hashima can be rough, and tours are frequently canceled due to high waves or bad weather conditions, sometimes even after the boat has departed Nagasaki Port. The tours on the day before were cancelled, so we didnt have high hopes....but we got lucky! We made it to the island and was even able to dock and get on the island (observation deck components only).



Yes, the tour is all in Japanese with English pamphlets...so just go in knowing that, and you'll be fine!

Visiting Hashima Island took a bit of effort to plan, so if it's something you're planning on seeing, I would recommend booking early. We tried booking our trip the week of Christmas week about 2 weeks in advance, and found only a few spots left on Klook. We had to move around our itinerary a bit around the available slots. About 2 days after we booked and paid, we were notified that our tour was cancelled. So we scrambled to find another operator, Gunkanjima Cruise Co, (you have to book through one of the few companies that do the boat tours there). The site is a bit outdated, so we werent sure if the booking went through, especially since payment is cash only on-site.



After we booked, we werent even sure if the trip was going to happen. The tours are weather dependent, as the seas around Hashima can be rough, and tours are frequently canceled due to high waves or bad weather conditions, sometimes even after the boat has departed Nagasaki Port. The tours on the day before were cancelled, so we didnt have high hopes....but we got lucky! We made it to the island and was even able to dock and get on the island (observation deck components only).



Yes, the tour is all in Japanese with English pamphlets...so just go in knowing that, and you'll be fine!

We walked from the station out across the bridge and to the main street of the Island. At 3pm on this warm and sunny day, there were lots of sightseers. A popular spot for couples and families to watch the setting sun.

We didn't have enough time to enjoy the beaches or aquarium but it would be very easy to fill a whole day with activities in this area. Especially with children!!

# Best Islands to Visit in Japan: Your Guide to the Country’s Hidden Gems

![Wayfairer Team](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/hs-fs/hubfs/Imported%20images/Social%20Media%20logo.png?width=50&height=50&name=Social%20Media%20logo.png)

Wayfairer Team December 08, 2025

![Time](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/hs-fs/hubfs/New%20Site%20Files/clock.png?width=20&height=20&name=clock.png)4 Min read

- [![Facebook](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/hs-fs/hubfs/New%20Site%20Files/facebook.png?width=30&height=30&name=facebook.png)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.wayfairertravel.com/inspiration/best-islands-to-visit-in-japan-luxury-vacation-guide/)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/hs-fs/hubfs/New%20Site%20Files/linkedin.png?width=30&height=30&name=linkedin.png)](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.wayfairertravel.com/inspiration/best-islands-to-visit-in-japan-luxury-vacation-guide/)
- [![back arrow](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/hs-fs/hubfs/New%20Site%20Files/new-back-arrow.png?width=10&height=17&name=new-back-arrow.png)Back](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/inspiration)

Japan’s archipelago comprises over 6,800 islands, each offering distinct landscapes, cultural experiences, and opportunities for luxury travel. While most visitors focus on the main island of Honshu, the best islands to visit in Japan extend far beyond Tokyo and Kyoto, revealing pristine beaches, volcanic hot springs, and centuries-old traditions that remain largely undiscovered by international travelers.

From the subtropical paradise of Okinawa to the rugged wilderness of Hokkaido, [Japan's islands](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/destinations/japan/) provide diverse experiences for discerning travelers seeking authentic cultural immersion and natural beauty. Whether you’re drawn to sacred pilgrimage sites, world-class diving, or exclusive ryokan retreats, Wayfairer can craft [luxury Japan vacations](https://www.wayfairertravel.com/destinations/japan/) around these spectacular island destinations.

## Discover Japan’s Island Diversity

The geographic range of Japan’s islands creates remarkable diversity in climate, culture, and landscape. The southernmost islands bask in tropical warmth, boasting coral reefs and white-sand beaches, while the northern territories offer dramatic coastlines, alpine terrain, and diverse wildlife viewing opportunities. This variation allows travelers to experience multiple climates and ecosystems within a single country.

Each island region has developed its own cultural identity, influenced by historical trade routes, indigenous populations, and geographic isolation. These distinct characteristics make island hopping an enriching way to understand Japan’s complexity beyond its metropolitan centers. The Japanese islands exemplify [how geography has shaped local cuisine](https://adhc.lib.ua.edu/globalfoodways/need-for-speed-geographys-effect-on-food/), dialects, crafts, and spiritual practices over the course of millennia.

For luxury travelers, this diversity translates into extraordinary possibilities for personalized itineraries. You might begin your journey diving among tropical fish in Okinawa’s turquoise waters, then transition to sampling Hokkaido’s renowned uni and sake in an intimate kaiseki setting, before concluding with meditation at a mountaintop temple accessible only by boat. The contrasts between islands create a richer, more nuanced understanding of Japanese culture than any single-destination trip could offer.

## 7 Beautiful Japan Islands to Add to Your Itinerary

1. Okinawa: The Okinawa archipelago serves as Japan’s tropical gateway, offering crystalline waters, vibrant coral reefs, and a unique Ryukyu culture distinct from that of mainland Japan. The region’s laid-back atmosphere, longevity-promoting cuisine, and historical sites provide a refreshing contrast to Japan’s fast-paced cities.
2. Hokkaido: Japan’s northernmost main island captivates visitors with its vast wilderness, volcanic landscapes, and exceptional powder snow. Beyond winter sports, Hokkaido offers summer flower fields, indigenous Ainu culture, and some of the country’s finest seafood and dairy products.
3. Naoshima: This small island in the Seto Inland Sea has transformed into an [international art destination](https://www.arts.gov/stories/blog/2023/few-our-favorite-museums-nea-crowdsourced-post), featuring contemporary museums, outdoor sculptures, and architectural installations. The harmonious blend of cutting-edge art with traditional island life creates an unparalleled cultural experience.
4. Miyajima: Home to the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, Miyajima ranks among Japan’s most photographed destinations. The sacred island prohibits permanent residence, but offers hiking trails, encounters with wild deer, and spectacular autumn foliage.
5. Yakushima: A UNESCO World Heritage site, [Yakushima](https://arboretum.harvard.edu/stories/ernest-henry-wilson-yakushima-and-the-wilson-stump/) enchants nature enthusiasts with its ancient cedar forests, many of which are over 1,000 years old. The mystical, moss-covered landscape inspired the setting for beloved animated films and provides exceptional hiking opportunities.
6. Ishigaki: This tropical island serves as a gateway to the Yaeyama archipelago, offering world-class diving, mangrove kayaking, and pristine beaches. The relaxed pace and natural beauty make it an ideal destination for luxury travelers seeking a secluded paradise.
7. Sado Island: Known for its historical gold mines and traditional performing arts, Sado Island has rich rural Japanese culture and stunning coastal scenery. The island’s taiko drumming tradition and seasonal festivals offer a deep cultural immersion experience.

The best islands to visit in Japan offer transformative experiences that extend far beyond typical tourist circuits. Let Wayfairer Travel create your personalized island adventure, revealing the hidden gems that make Japan’s archipelago truly extraordinary.

In this article, **[Japan Shore Excursions](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/)** will take you beyond Tokyo and Kyoto to explore the most unforgettable **islands in Japan** to visit. Imagine stepping onto sacred shores where a floating torii gate rises from the sea, wandering through art-filled villages, or relaxing on tropical beaches with crystal-clear waters. With more than 6,000 islands waiting to be discovered, your cruise ship becomes the gateway to Japan’s hidden gems and to memories you’ll treasure forever.

## Top Islands in Japan to Visit from Cruise Ships

Discover the best islands in Japan to visit on a cruise: Miyajima’s floating torii, Naoshima’s art, Ishigaki’s beaches, and Yakushima’s forests. Find your perfect island escape with Japan Shore Excursions.

### Miyajima (Itsukushima): The Island of the Gods

![Miyajima - top islands in Japan to visit](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Miyajima-top-islands-in-Japan-to-visit.jpg)

Often called the “Island of the Gods,” Miyajima is where Japan’s spiritual heart meets natural landscapes. With its floating torii gate rising from the sea and lush mountain backdrop, it’s no wonder travelers rank it among the best islands in Japan to visit. Here, centuries-old traditions blend with breathtaking scenery, offering a perfect mix for culture seekers and nature lovers alike. At Japan Shore Excursions, we bring you closer to this timeless beauty with guides who know the island’s hidden stories.

For cruise passengers, Miyajima is one of the easiest and most rewarding side trips. With a short **[tour from Hiroshima Port](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/port/hiroshima-shore-excursions/)**, the island offers a full experience in a single day. You can explore sacred sites, enjoy scenic walks, and return to your ship with memories to last a lifetime. Few Japanese islands to visit combine accessibility and cultural depth as seamlessly as Miyajima.

_**Top Things to Do & See on Miyajima:**_

Itsukushima Shrine: Marvel at the world-famous “floating” vermilion torii gate, a UNESCO World Heritage icon that seems to rise straight from the sea.

- Catch a golden sunset: Watch the Seto Inland Sea glow gold and crimson, a view that proves why Miyajima is counted among the best Japanese islands to visit.
- Lose yourself in mystical trails: Stroll through ancient temples and cedar-lined forest paths, where friendly deer roam freely.
- Taste the island’s flavors: Wander Omotesando shopping street and savor grilled oysters, seafood skewers, and sweet momiji manju cakes, an experience that makes Miyajima one of the best islands in Japan to visit.
- Witness seasonal magic: Visit in spring for cherry blossoms or in autumn for fiery maple leaves painting the island in color.

### Ishigaki (Yaeyama Islands): Okinawa’s Pristine Escape

![Ishigaki - the most beautiful island in Japan](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Ishigaki-the-most-beautiful-island-in-Japan.jpg)

Swapping temple roofs for turquoise seas and coral reefs, among the Okinawa islands to visit, Ishigaki shines as the ultimate tropical escape. Often called the jewel of the Yaeyama Islands, Ishigaki offers more than postcard views. It’s where crystal-clear seas meet vibrant Okinawan culture. From world - class snorkeling to authentic island villages, it’s easy to see why many consider it one of the best islands in Japan to visit for both relaxation and adventure.

As a key port in the Yaeyama Islands, Ishigaki is highly convenient for cruise visitors. **[Ishigaki shore excursions](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/port/ishigaki-shore-excursions/)** can include snorkeling, beach time, and cultural explorations, all within easy reach of the port. Ishigaki is more than a pretty beach, it’s an island full of activities that promise lasting memories:

- Snorkel or dive in Kabira Bay: Emerald-green waters and manta rays make this a must among the Okinawa islands to visit.
- Relax on Yonehara or Sukuji Beach: Soft white sands prove why Ishigaki is often called the most beautiful islands in Japan.
- Explore Ishigaki Yaima Village: Traditional houses and folk culture show why it’s one of the best Japanese islands to visit.
- Hike Mt. Nosoko: Panoramic views reveal Ishigaki’s unspoiled beauty, making it a highlight among Japanese islands to visit.
- Island-hop to Taketomi: A charming village nearby with sandy lanes and buffalo carts for a timeless Okinawan experience that shows why Ishigaki and its neighbors are some of the most unique islands in Japan.

### Izu Oshima: A Volcanic Adventure Near Tokyo

![Izu Oshima - Japanese island near Tokyo](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Izu-Oshima-Japanese-island-near-Tokyo.jpg)

Among the many Japanese islands near Tokyo, Izu Oshima is a true standout. With its volcanic landscapes, black-sand beaches, and unique traditions, it’s often praised as one of most beautiful island in Japan for thrill-seekers and nature lovers alike.

With easy access from Tokyo Bay, this island is ideal for cruise passengers. In a single **[shore excursion from Yokohama port](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/port/yokohama-shore-excursions/)**, you can hike a volcano, soak in hot springs, and savor island delicacies before returning to your ship. Few islands in Japan to visit promise such an adventurous escape so close to the capital. Here are the highlights that prove why it’s a highlight spots for adventure:

- Climb Mount Mihara: Hike across lava fields and stand at the rim of an active volcano for unforgettable crater views.
- Wander Ura-Sabaku Desert: Experience Japan’s only desert, like landscape, a surreal gem among volcanic islands in Japan.
- Relax in outdoor baths overlooking the Pacific Ocean
- Taste local flavors: From fresh seafood to camellia-flavored sweets, the cuisine is as distinctive as the island’s terrain.

### Naoshima: Japan's Island of Art

![Naoshima - Islands in Japan for Art](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Naoshima-Islands-in-Japan-for-Art.jpg)

Among the many art islands in Japan, Naoshima is the undisputed star. Frequently described as the best island in Japan to visit for creativity, it offers a rare blend of culture, innovation, and coastal beauty. Naoshima is more than an island. It’s an open-air museum where nature and art coexist.

Thanks to easy access from the ports of Okayama and Takamatsu, Naoshima is ideal for a one-day shore excursion. The island’s compact size makes it effortless to explore world-class museums, waterfront sculptures, and charming villages, all without worrying about travel logistics.

_**Naoshima’s highlights make it a must-see among art islands in Japan:**_

- Chichu Art Museum: A subterranean masterpiece housing Monet’s Water Lilies alongside works by James Turrell and Walter De Maria.
- Benesse House Museum: Where modern art seamlessly merges with the island’s natural beauty.
- Yayoi Kusama’s Pumpkins: Iconic seaside sculptures that have become symbols of Naoshima’s creative spirit.
- Honmura Art House Project: Abandoned homes reborn as immersive art spaces that surprise at every turn, making Naoshima one of the most inspiring art islands in Japan.

### Yakushima: A Mystical UNESCO World Heritage Site

![Yakushima Island from Kagoshima port](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Yakushima-Island-from-Kagoshima-port.jpg)

Among the many Japanese islands to visit, Yakushima is truly one of a kind. Celebrated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site Japan, this lush subtropical island off Kyushu is often chosen by travelers who seek untouched nature, serenity, and spiritual renewal.

Yakushima is more than an island, it’s a living, breathing time capsule of nature. With towering cedar trees thousands of years old and an ecosystem teeming with wildlife, it’s a paradise for hikers, dreamers, and anyone looking for the best Japanese island to visit for natural wonder.

With **[Kagoshima shore excursions](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/port/kagoshima-shore-excursions/)**, Yakushima’s highlights will leave you in awe of nature’s power and poetry:

- Trek Shiratani Unsuikyo Forest: A mossy wonderland that inspired Studio Ghibli’s Princess Mononoke, making Yakushima a top UNESCO World Heritage Site Japan.
- See the legendary Jōmon Sugi: A massive cedar tree estimated to be over 7,000 years old, a living symbol of resilience.
- Visit Oko-no-taki Waterfall: One of Japan’s most powerful waterfalls, cascading 88 meters into a dramatic gorge.
- Spot Yakushima’s wildlife: From playful macaques to gentle deer, the island’s animals thrive in their natural habitat.
- Absorb the island’s mystique: Mist, moss, and rain create an atmosphere that reminds travelers why Yakushima is often called the most beautiful island in Japan and one of the most magical UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Japan

## Planning Your Island Visit from a Japanese Cruise Port

A Japanese cruise isn’t just about vibrant cities. It’s your gateway to unforgettable island shore excursions in Japan. To make the most of your day trip, here’s how to plan wisely from your docking port.

### Choose the Right Island for Your Port

![Choose the right island to visit in Japan](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Choose-the-right-island-to-visit-in-Japan.jpg)

The right choice depends on where your ship anchors. From Japanese cruise ports, Miyajima is the perfect excursion from Hiroshima, while the volcanic Izu Islands are easily reached from Tokyo. Matching the island to your port ensures a smoother, stress-free adventure.

### Make the Most of Your Cruise Schedule

Cruise schedules can be tight, so factor in ferry or transfer times. For most travelers, compact itineraries work best. Choosing the best Japanese island to visit near your port lets you maximize the day and still return comfortably before departure.

### Why Guided Japan Shore Excursions Are the Smart Choice?

![Join guided shore excursions to Japanese islands](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Join-guided-shore-excursions-to-Japanese-islands.jpg)

Exploring on your own can be tricky but with a guided tour, every detail is handled. Local experts in Japan shore excursions manage transportation, timing, and logistics, giving you peace of mind while you enjoy the sights

### What to Pack for Island Shore Excursions in Japan

A little preparation goes a long way. Bring:

- Sunscreen and a hat: Essential for outdoor activities under the island sun.
- Comfortable walking shoes: Perfect for shrine paths, forest trails, or seaside strolls.
- Swimwear: A must if your excursion takes you to Okinawa or Ishigaki’s turquoise beaches, two of the most beautiful Japanese islands to visit.
- Local currency (Yen): Handy for food stalls, small shops, and souvenir markets.

Japan’s islands offer more than scenery, they bring you closer to the country’s soul. From the floating torii of Miyajima to the art museums of Naoshima, the tropical charm of Ishigaki, and the mystical forests of Yakushima, each destination proves why these are the most [**beautiful islands in Japan**](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/?p=28833&preview=true) to visit.
